The Battle of Turkistan is a battle that occurred in 1652, by the Khoshut commander Galdamba of Khoshut Khanate, in assistance of the Dzungar Khanate against the Kazakh Khanate's leader, Jangir khan killing him in battle.
During the Kazakh–Dzungar War (1635–1658), the Khong tayiji of the Dzungars, Erdeni batur invaded the Kazakh Khanate and captured Jangir Khan as POW at the Erdeni's first campaign. Later after he was released — Erdeni continued his offensives and plundered the Syr Darya region, Jangir khan asked Yalangto'sh Bakhodir for assistance for the Battle of Orbulaq, defeating the Dzungar army. With a defeat by the Kazakhs, Erdeni Batur had asked Galdamba batur of the Khoshuts to campaign against them, which he agreed and sent out with 3,000 men. The young commander first intercepted Jangir's army at the city of Turkistan, then he charged at the Kazakhs leading to a fierce battle, during that Jangir Khan was killed in battle whilst the Kazakhs presumably suffered heavy casualties from the battle. This opened Galdamba to campaign on the Alatau region until an Uzbek relief force arrived at Chu river.
